subject: Private VPC pricing — follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Jason Lee <jason.lee@fintechco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.example.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC pricing — follow-up & next steps

Thanks again for the time today, Jason — great conversation on FintechCo's latency and compliance requirements. Quick recap and next steps from my side.

Key takeaways from the discovery call:
- Workload: customer-facing fraud scoring + post-authorize chat summaries. Tight P50 latency target (~150ms token) for inference.
- Expected steady-state usage: ~3M tokens/month initially, with spikes/bursts up to ~10M/month; growth plan to ~15-20M over 12 months.
- Compliance: SOC2 required, customer-managed VPC (Private) preferred, multiple environments (prod + staging + dev).
- Procurement: procurement team will own licensing discussion; target procurement window: end of month.

Pricing/qualification items we need to lock down:
1) Token volume commitments (monthly committed tokens vs burst/overage expectations)
2) Target unit economics — target $/1M tokens you’re comfortable with for committed tier
3) Environment count (prod/staging/dev + any DR/region copies)
4) Support tier (Standard vs Premium 24x7 SLA)

Attached: Private_VPC_pricing_summary.pdf (high-level options), MA_template.docx (master agreement template). I also attached a draft quote spreadsheet (Redwood_Private_Quote_v1.xlsx) for the numbers below.

High-level options (rough, ballpark today):
- Annual subscription (recommended for Private/VPC): base platform license $100,000/year (includes up to 2 environments), additional environment: $15,000/year each.
- Support: Standard (business hours, included), Premium (24x7 + 4hr incident SLA) = +18% of annual license.
- Usage pricing (inference tokens): committed-commit pricing: $6,500 per 1M tokens (for committed tiers >=10M/month), overage/elastic rate: $9,000 per 1M tokens. For smaller commits (<=5M), committed pricing sits around $8,000 per 1M.

Questions for you before I prepare a formal quote:
- Can you confirm the committed tokens you’re willing to commit to month 1 vs expected steady state?
- How many environments do you need (prod/staging/dev/DR)?
- Do you want Premium support out of the gate?

Next steps: once we have those items we’ll produce a formal quote (with line items for license, environments, support, and committed token pricing) + a draft SOW and procurement-friendly summary. Ben (cc’d) will help validate infra and CI/CD details for the Private install.

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.example.com
From: Jason Lee <jason.lee@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.example.com>, FintechCo Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC pricing — follow-up & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. Internal notes / answers below.

- Token volumes: initial pilot ~1-3M tokens/month (Q2), production ramp to ~15M/month within 6-9 months, planning for up to 20M/month by EOY. We can commit to a 15M/month committed tier once procurement and infra signoff are complete (want a 3-month ramp cadence).
- Budget: target spend is roughly $15k-25k/month initially (we understand this will expand as volume ramps). Our procurement team is targeting an average committed unit cost of ~$9k/1M tokens — we can be flexible if licensing/support tradeoffs reduce total TCO.
- Environments: prod + staging + dev (3 total). We may need a DR read-only copy in another region depending on the final architecture — tentatively +1.
- Support: interested in Premium (24x7 SLA) given real-time fraud implications.

Action items from our side:
- Procurement (cc’d) will pull the vendor onboarding/compliance checklist and SOC2 evidence requests — please send details.
- Ben — any infra constraints you want to flag for the Private install?

If you can shoot over a formal quote with the licensing + committed token price deck, and a procurement-ready summary (SOC2, data flow, logging, SLAs), we’ll prioritize review this week.

Thanks,

Jason
Director of ML Engineering | FintechCo
jason.lee@fintechco.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Jason Lee <jason.lee@fintechco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC pricing — follow-up & next steps

Appreciate the details, Jason — this is very helpful. Based on the numbers you gave, here's a recommended quote structure (I’ll attach an updated spreadsheet to the DocuSign link).

Recommended commercial structure (Private / VPC):
- Annual Subscription (recommended):
  - Base platform license: $100,000/year (includes up to 2 environments)
  - Additional environment: $15,000/year each (3rd environment = +$15,000)
  - Premium Support: +18% of annual license (~$21,600/year on $120k license) — includes 24x7 coverage, 4-hr P1 SLA, quarterly architecture reviews.

- Token economics (inference):
  Option A — Committed tier (best for predictable TCO): commit to 15M tokens/month -> price = $6,500 per 1M tokens (committed rate).
    - 15M/month => monthly token charge = 15 * $6,500 = $97,500/month (note: examples are normalized; we can structure as an annual usage commitment with monthly billing or monthly true-ups)
  Option B — Lower commit (step): commit to 5M/month => $8,000 per 1M tokens; overage above commit billed at $9,500 per 1M.
  Option C — On-prem CPU/GPU bring-your-own-hardware: reduced usage price (baseline $5,000 per 1M) but higher upfront engineering/setup fee and license floor.

Interpretation relative to your target: your target ~$9k/1M is in-band with Option B (smaller commit). For a 15M committed tier (Option A) we can get you below that target but it requires the committed term. We can also structure a 6-9 month ramp with graduated commit discounts.

Procurement and compliance deliverables we will include in the procurement pack:
- SOC2 report (Redwood Inference), architecture diagram for VPC deployment, data flow and retention overview, KMS/HSM integration details, audit log sampling, and network requirements for onsite private control plane.

Requested confirmations so I can finalize a formal quote:
1) Confirm committed tokens for year 1 (pilot months vs steady state). Based on call I’ll draft 3 scenarios (5M, 10M, 15M committed).
2) Confirm final environment count (you noted 3 + maybe DR) — please confirm whether to include DR as part of initial quote.
3) Confirm Premium support yes/no.

If you confirm those 3 items, I’ll create a procurement-ready quote and pull the SOC2 & compliance packet into a shared Drive link + send a DocuSign quote. Ben will follow up on infra/installation notes (cc’d).

Proposed next meeting: 30-minute procurement + architecture sync — suggest Wed 24 Mar or Thu 25 Mar (I’ll send a calendar hold once you confirm availability).

Attachments: updated quote spreadsheet (Redwood_Private_Quote_v1.xlsx) — per above.

Thanks — will aim to get the formal quote in your hands within 48 hours of confirmations.

Best,

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.example.com

Subject: Re: Private VPC pricing — follow-up & next steps

Marissa — confirmed on our side:
- Environments: 3 (prod / staging / dev). Please include DR as an optional line item (we will decide after the architecture sync).
- Support: Premium (yes).
- Committed tokens: target 15M/month as the committed tier (we may ramp over first 3 months). Procurement will review the quote and we aim to complete onboarding by the end of the month.

Ben — I’ll sync with you offline on infra constraints; if anything blocks the Private install we’ll flag it to Marissa ASAP.

Thanks,

Jason
